title: God's kingdom is near
summary: Jesus announces the kingdom's nearness and summons repentance and faith in the good news.

title: Called to follow
summary: Jesus calls Simon and Andrew to follow him and envisages a mission involving others.

title: Show yourself to the priest
summary: Jesus instructs a healed man to present himself to a priest and offer what Moses prescribed.

title: Calling sinners
summary: Jesus defends eating with stigmatized people by comparing his mission to that of a physician.

title: Fasting and new wineskins
summary: Jesus uses a bridegroom, cloth and wineskins to explain different fasting practices.

title: Sabbath for humanity
summary: Jesus speaks of the Sabbath's purpose for people and of the Son of Man's authority over it.

title: Doing good on the Sabbath
summary: Jesus challenges opponents to consider whether Sabbath behavior should save or harm life.

title: Who belongs to Jesus' family?
summary: Jesus defines his family by doing God's will rather than biological relationship alone.

title: Parable of the sower
summary: Jesus tells a story of seeds in different soils producing different outcomes.

title: Explaining the sower
summary: Jesus interprets the soils as responses to the word, including distraction by riches.

title: Seed grows beyond the sower
summary: Jesus portrays God's kingdom as seed that grows and eventually is harvested.

title: Mustard seed
summary: Jesus depicts the kingdom through the growth of a very small seed.

title: Tell of mercy received
summary: Jesus directs a restored man to tell people at home what the Lord has done for him.

title: Hospitality and rejection in mission
summary: Jesus directs the Twelve to stay in a hosting home and depart from places refusing them.

title: Commandment versus tradition
summary: Jesus uses scripture and the example of Corban to criticize traditions that obstruct duties to parents.

title: External things and defilement
summary: Jesus tells the crowd that what enters a person is not the central source of moral defilement.

title: Defilement comes from the heart
summary: Jesus tells the disciples that destructive conduct arises from within; narrative framing in 7:19 is textually significant.
caution: The clause at Mark 7:19 is punctuated as narrator comment in many modern editions; examine Greek syntax before ascribing it all to Jesus.

title: Children's bread and outsiders
summary: Jesus responds to a Gentile mother's request through an image of children and bread.

title: Response to the Gentile mother
summary: Jesus responds positively to the woman's reply and tells her that her daughter has been released.

title: Taking up the cross
summary: Jesus summons the crowd and disciples to costly allegiance, self-denial, and evaluating worldly gain.

title: Greatness as service
summary: Jesus defines the first as a servant and uses the welcome of a child to illustrate receiving him.

title: Don't obstruct an outsider
summary: Jesus instructs the disciples not to stop someone working in his name and affirms support offered to them.

title: Marriage and separation
summary: Jesus responds to questions about divorce by invoking creation and warning against separating what God joins.

title: Divorce and remarriage
summary: Jesus gives the disciples a further statement connecting divorce and remarriage with adultery.

title: Welcome children
summary: Jesus insists that children be welcomed and links receiving the kingdom to their example.

title: A rich man's call
summary: Jesus cites commandments and calls a particular wealthy person to sell his possessions, give to the poor and follow.

title: Riches and entering the kingdom
summary: Jesus warns about difficulty for wealthy people entering the kingdom and concludes with God's possibility.

title: Authority and service
summary: Jesus contrasts the domination of rulers with service among his followers, relating it to his mission.

title: Temple as prayer for all nations
summary: Jesus cites scripture and criticizes temple practices as contrary to its calling.

title: Prayer, trust and forgiveness
summary: Jesus encourages faithful prayer and instructs disciples to forgive when praying.

title: Caesar and God
summary: Jesus answers an attempted trap about taxes by distinguishing claims connected to Caesar and to God.

title: Love God and neighbor
summary: Jesus identifies love for God and neighbor as central commandments, citing Israel's scriptures.

title: Warning about religious elites
summary: Jesus criticizes religious status-seeking and exploitation of widows.

title: Widow's offering
summary: Jesus calls attention to a poor widow giving from necessity rather than surplus; whether praise or critique is disputed.
caution: Interpretation of the widow scene is disputed: commendation of generosity and criticism of an exploitative context are both argued.

title: Do not be misled by crisis
summary: Jesus warns against messianic impostors and panic during wars and upheavals.

title: Timing unknown, remain watchful
summary: Jesus says the timing of the coming day is unknown and commands watchfulness.

title: Anointing and care for the poor
summary: Jesus defends a woman's costly act and observes that opportunities to aid the poor continue.

title: Bread, cup and covenant
summary: Jesus associates bread and cup with his body, covenant, and future kingdom participation.
caution: Comparison with Luke's supper tradition must account for textual and liturgical history; this entry does not settle those debates.

title: Prayer in Gethsemane
summary: Jesus addresses God in distress and subordinates his desire to God's will.

title: Watch and pray under trial
summary: Jesus calls the disciples to alertness and prayer against temptation.

title: Identity before the council
summary: Jesus replies to questioning about messianic identity and the Son of Man's vindication.

title: Kingdom proclaimed
summary: Jesus calls for repentance as Matthew opens his account of public ministry.

title: Called to become fishers of people
summary: Jesus invites Simon and Andrew to follow and enter a mission involving others.

title: Blessings and the people of the kingdom
summary: Jesus describes persons receiving divine favor in a series of blessings that differ from Luke's formulation.

title: Salt and light
summary: Jesus uses salt and light to portray visible responsibility among disciples.

title: Law and fulfillment
summary: Matthew depicts Jesus rejecting abolition of Law and Prophets and speaking of their fulfillment.

title: Anger and reconciliation
summary: Jesus places anger and reconciliation within the obligations associated with the prohibition of murder.

title: Adultery and intention
summary: Jesus intensifies moral scrutiny to include desire and employs severe imagery about avoiding wrongdoing.

title: Divorce and remarriage
summary: Jesus treats divorce and remarriage within the mountain discourse, with qualifications that differ across Gospels.

title: Let yes be yes
summary: Jesus challenges oath-taking and directs hearers toward straightforward truthful speech.

title: Retaliation and generosity
summary: Jesus counters retaliatory norms with nonretaliation and giving.

title: Love enemies
summary: Jesus instructs disciples to love and pray for opponents as an expression of divine generosity.

title: Giving privately
summary: Jesus warns against public performance of almsgiving and emphasizes the motive of giving.

title: A pattern of prayer
summary: Jesus gives a prayer addressed to the Father, relating divine rule, daily provision, forgiveness and testing.
caution: Some manuscript traditions append a doxology to the model prayer; consult the primary edition's notes and a critical apparatus before quoting a standardized ending.

title: Forgiving others
summary: Jesus connects the granting and withholding of forgiveness with the hearers' treatment of others.

title: Fasting without display
summary: Jesus contrasts outward performance of fasting with practice not designed to impress observers.

title: Treasure and attachment
summary: Jesus warns against storing earthly treasure and connects treasure with the heart.

title: Two competing masters
summary: Jesus presents service to God and wealth as rival allegiances.

title: Worry and the kingdom
summary: Jesus uses birds and plants to warn against preoccupation with necessities while directing attention to the kingdom.

title: Judgment and self-examination
summary: Jesus warns against condemning others without first recognizing one's own faults.

title: Ask, seek and knock
summary: Jesus encourages persistent petition through an analogy involving parental care.

title: The rule of reciprocity
summary: Jesus tells hearers to treat others as they would wish to be treated.

title: The narrow gate
summary: Jesus portrays the path leading to life as difficult to find.

title: Teachers known by fruit
summary: Jesus warns about misleading prophets and uses fruit-bearing trees to describe discernment.

title: Actions beyond profession
summary: Jesus warns that verbal allegiance is insufficient apart from doing the Father's will.

title: Houses on differing foundations
summary: Jesus closes the discourse with builders as a picture of hearing and acting on instruction.

title: Present yourself to the priest
summary: After healing, Jesus directs a man to follow the requirements associated with priestly inspection.

title: The centurion and confidence
summary: Jesus answers a centurion's request for healing and comments on his trust.

title: Mercy and those considered sinners
summary: Jesus answers criticism of table fellowship with an analogy about a physician and a call to mercy.

title: Pray for workers in the harvest
summary: Jesus tells disciples the harvest is great while workers are scarce and urges prayer.

title: Mission and hospitality
summary: Jesus instructs the Twelve concerning their mission, provisions, healings, hospitality and refusal.

title: Opposition to messengers
summary: Jesus describes followers facing hostile institutions and needing guidance under pressure.

title: Fearlessness and public witness
summary: Jesus encourages disciples to witness openly despite threats and costs.

title: Conflicting family loyalties
summary: Jesus describes social division and demanding allegiance in the face of family obligations.

title: Receiving the sent
summary: Jesus connects hospitality shown to messengers with the reception of the one who sent them.

title: Answering John's messengers
summary: Jesus replies to the Baptist's messengers with references to works of healing and proclamation.

title: Thanks and rest
summary: Jesus thanks the Father and invites burdened hearers to learn his gentle way.

title: Mercy and the Sabbath
summary: Jesus defends conduct on the Sabbath through an appeal to mercy and the Son of Man's authority.

title: A divided kingdom cannot stand
summary: Jesus rebuts allegations about his power by arguing against self-defeating division.

title: The sign of Jonah
summary: Jesus responds to a demand for a sign with a Jonah comparison and a judgment warning.

title: Those who do the Father's will
summary: Jesus identifies kinship with those who do his heavenly Father's will.

title: Sower and soil
summary: Jesus tells a parable of seed falling on several kinds of ground.

title: Wheat and weeds
summary: Jesus tells a parable about mixed growth and delaying separation until harvest.

title: Mustard seed and leaven
summary: Jesus uses two small beginnings with wide effects to picture the kingdom.

title: Hidden treasure and precious pearl
summary: Jesus compares the kingdom's worth to decisive choices made for remarkable discoveries.

title: The net and the catch
summary: Jesus compares a wide catch and later sorting with judgment at the end of the age.

title: What makes people unclean
summary: Jesus argues that morally defiling deeds and words arise from the heart rather than simply from food or ritual handling.

title: A Canaanite woman's appeal
summary: Jesus and a Gentile woman exchange words over his mission's priority and her daughter's healing.

title: Peter's confession and the keys
summary: Jesus questions the disciples about his identity and describes Peter's role using rock and keys imagery.

title: Take up the cross
summary: Jesus calls followers to self-denial and reframes what it means to gain or lose one's life.

title: Status and a child
summary: Jesus answers a question of greatness by making a child the example of kingdom stature.

title: Reconciliation and communal decisions
summary: Jesus sets out responses to wrongdoing and speaks of community agreement and gathering.

title: Forgive repeatedly
summary: Jesus answers Peter's question about repeated forgiveness with an expansive response.

title: Debt forgiven and mercy denied
summary: Jesus illustrates the consequences of refusing mercy after receiving mercy oneself.

title: Marriage and divorce
summary: Jesus responds to opponents through creation texts and a contested exception concerning divorce.

title: Let children come
summary: Jesus tells followers not to prevent children approaching him.

title: The wealthy seeker
summary: Jesus directs a wealthy questioner to relinquish possessions and follow, then warns of wealth's obstacles.

title: Laborers paid unexpectedly
summary: Jesus describes a landowner paying laborers in a way that challenges claims of comparative merit.

title: Greatness through service
summary: Jesus contrasts rulers wielding power with service and self-giving.

title: A house of prayer
summary: Jesus invokes Scripture while challenging the use of the temple.

title: Two sons and actual response
summary: Jesus compares promised obedience and enacted obedience while confronting religious critics.

title: Tenants and accountability
summary: Jesus tells a vineyard story that criticizes those entrusted with it and speaks of a rejected stone.

title: A wedding banquet and the invitation
summary: Jesus tells a parable about rejected invitations, unexpected guests and judgment.

title: Caesar and God
summary: Jesus answers a question about tribute with competing claims of civic and divine allegiance.

title: Life and resurrection
summary: Jesus rebuts a hypothetical about marriage through argument concerning resurrection and God's faithfulness.

title: The first and second commandments
summary: Jesus names love of God and love of neighbor as essential to Law and Prophets.

title: Status and humility in teaching
summary: Jesus warns about religious status, titles and the contrast between serving and being honored.

title: Woes and misdirected religious leadership
summary: Jesus delivers harsh criticism of hypocrisy and harmful religious behavior.

title: Warnings and endurance
summary: Jesus addresses deception, upheaval and perseverance while speaking of future events.

title: The fig tree and nearness
summary: Jesus uses seasonal growth to describe signs and the enduring significance of his words.

title: Prepared bridesmaids
summary: Jesus uses a wedding scene to illustrate the urgency of remaining prepared.

title: Entrusted wealth and accountability
summary: Jesus tells of servants judged on handling resources entrusted to them.

title: Final judgment and vulnerable people
summary: Jesus depicts judgment through treatment of people facing hunger, exclusion, illness and imprisonment.
caution: The identity of the people described as 'the least of these' is debated. A narrated judgment scene should not be treated as a modern policy blueprint.

title: Bread and cup at the final meal
summary: Jesus interprets bread and cup during the meal and speaks of the covenant and coming kingdom.

title: Prayer before arrest
summary: Jesus prays that the coming ordeal may pass while submitting to the Father's will.

title: Commission to teach the nations
summary: The risen Jesus charges his followers with making disciples and teaching obedience in all nations.
caution: The narrated post-resurrection commission is distinct from Matthew's pre-resurrection mission instructions in chapter 10, and Gospel commission accounts should not be merged into a single verbatim speech.
